comments.body: What I've noticed when testing this is that when there's only one triple in the delete clause, it seems to work fine. Two or more seems to be where it's running into trouble.
FWIW, I'm seeing the same behavior on the master branch.

Testing with "git bisect" has revealed that this issue was introduced between Fedora 4.4.0 and 4.5.0 with the following commit:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/8cceaebd0121c34e6b9c156f4d119398d58a1ad4
FWIW, I grabbed the Jetty releases for 4.4. and 4.5 and ran the above scripts against them. I can confirm Andrew Woods's finding with 'git bisect'. 4.4 does not contain the bug but 4.5 does.

Andrew Woods et al : Interesting note: it appears that Chris Beer disabled the unit tests covering this section of the code back in 2014.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/test/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/utils/NodePropertiesToolsTest.java#L64

from git blame fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/test/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/utils/NodePropertiesToolsTest.java

46a43bfd fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/test/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/utils/NodePropertiesToolsTest.java (Chris Beer 2014-10-05 08:51:37 -0700 64) @Ignore

Does anyone have any recollection of why the @Ignore? Or just an oversight?
That was back in 4.0.0-beta... likely due to the headache of managing too many Mocks.
Andrew Woods: What do you recommend? Shall I continue to ignore it or attempt to fix the broken unit tests?
I would suggest focusing on adding one or more integration tests to FedoraLdpIT.java that resemble the example in this ticket.

Andrew Woods: Regarding the solution - removing the following line causes Bethany's scripts to produce the expected output.

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/utils/NodePropertiesTools.java#L240

It seems unnecessary to throw an exception if an attempt to remove a non-existent property value.

The reason calls are coming in to remove non-existent property values appears to be due to the jena layer generating duplicate triples to be deleted. I don't understand enough of the fundamentals of Jena to understand why the query engine does what it does but I can say the duplicated bindings originate here: https://github.com/apache/jena/blob/master/jena-arq/src/main/java/org/apache/jena/sparql/modify/UpdateEngineWorker.java#L556
Andrew Woods: Okay - I'll refrain from trying to fix the @Ignored unit tests.
This looks good. Bethany Seeger / Jared Whiklo, please merge if you are satisfied.

renderedFields.description:
Given a resource with these triples:

<> <http://example.org/test/x> "x" .
<> <http://example.org/test/y> "y" .

<> <http://example.org/test/a> "1" .
<> <http://example.org/test/a> "2" .
<> <http://example.org/test/a> "3" .
<> <http://example.org/test/a> "4" .

<> <http://example.org/test/b> "1" .
<> <http://example.org/test/b> "2" .
<> <http://example.org/test/b> "3" .
<> <http://example.org/test/b> "4" .

<> <http://example.org/test/c> "1" .
<> <http://example.org/test/c> "2" .
<> <http://example.org/test/c> "3" .
<> <http://example.org/test/c> "4" .

The following SPARQL delete pattern will result in a 400 Bad Request error and the triples are not deleted.

DELETE WHERE

{ <> <http://example.org/test/a> ?a . <> <http://example.org/test/b> ?b . }

I've included two bash scripts that reproduce the results. One contains the above DELETE Sparql pattern the other uses a variant.

This issue may be related to the problem described here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/fedora-community/oDcMOBAh9nY
